column1: # boru Language Specification: FOLD / MAP / FILTER / SORT and the collection
# words, in the shapes REAL programs spell them.
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# Family: fold-map-filter. Written to widen the corpus past the one-liner
# shapes it had: every fold call form and accumulator kind (scalar, String,
# List, Map); bodies written as a literal quotation, as a def-bound word, as
# a def-bound fn VALUE, as a `=>` lambda and as a closure over an enclosing
# binding; filter in all three predicate forms (quotation, Reach lens,
# Function callback) over lists and over maps; sort / reverse / take / shed /
# flatten / size; sorting BY A COMPUTED KEY (boru has no comparator sort —
# ArrayUtil.sortby / ArrayUtil.grade are the idiom); and chained pipelines
# that put each, filter, fold and sort in one statement, inside a fn, over
# records, over class instances and over module results.
# EVERY row's expected column is the engine's OWN answer, captured from
# `boru do -no-compile '<input> end canon'` — the INTERPRETER, and the same
# canon rendering the spec runner compares against. Nothing here is guessed.
# `-no-compile` is load-bearing: `boru do` defaults to compile-try, and one
# candidate row (noted in §12) answers differently on the two engines.
# ROWS THAT FAIL TO COMPILE TO COMPILE ARE RECORDED DELIBERATELY, as OPEN DEFECTS.
# Their descriptions carry the exact reason `BORU_FORCE_COMPILE=1` printed.
# A compile compile failure is WHOLE-PROGRAM and latches on the FIRST unsupported
# construct, which is why the compiler scores ~96% on a corpus of 40-character
# one-liners and ~65% on real files that combine constructs. These rows are
# the gap made visible; they are not mistakes and must not be deleted to make
# a ceiling green.
# NOTE FOR THE RATCHET: test/go/langspec/compiled_coverage_test.go holds
# failureCeiling = 0. The declining rows below are NEW EVIDENCE, not
# regressions — the ceiling must be re-based (or this file moved under
# lang/spec/frontier/) when the corpus is next gated.
# A note on ARGUMENT ORDER, because it decides what a fold body means: a call
# binds its arguments in SIGNATURE order, filling positions from the forward
# stack first and the value stack afterwards, top-first. fold pushes the
# accumulator and then the ELEMENT on top of it, so a two-argument word in the
# body sees (element, accumulator) as (top, deeper) — `0 fold [sub] [1 2 3]`
# is acc-minus-element all the way down, and `'' fold ([a e] => [a add e])`
# does NOT concatenate left-to-right (§4).
# §1  fold — the call forms, with and without an initial accumulator
0 fold [add] [1 2 3 4]
